_For Tier 1:_

* _If a driver’s account is blocked due to verification, send the following message:_
* _(FR) Vous n’avez pas réussi le processus de vérification faciale. Conformément à l’article 13.5 de nos Conditions Générales d’Utilisation, votre compte est bloqué. Si vous n’êtes pas d’accord avec cette décision, vous pouvez fournir des précisions dans cette conversation._
* _(ENG): You have not passed the facial verification process. In accordance with article 13.5 of our General Conditions of Use, your account is blocked. If you do not agree with this decision, you can provide clarification here._
* _Escalate to Tier 2._

_For Tier 2:_

* _Check the images and blocking reason on Beehive to confirm whether:_
_a. Needs to be escalated to Verification Support as verification should be triggered again._
_b. If the block will remain due to suspicious activity._



*_Note_*_: Ensure at least 30 minutes have passed between the 1st macro and the sending of the 2nd macro._



_Based on the outcome, give one of the two following replies:_



*_a. Notification after successful review_*

_(ENG) “Thank you for contacting us regarding the outcome of the facial verification process. After verification by our Customer Support following your contestation of the decision, we are happy to trigger the verification process again so you can take another selfie verification”._

_(FR) “Nous vous remercions de nous avoir contactés au sujet du résultat de la procédure de vérification faciale. Après contrôle par notre Service Qualité suite à votre contestation de la décision, nous sommes en mesure de lancer une nouvelle vérification faciale que vous recevrez prochainement.”_



*_b. Notification after unsuccessful review_* 

_(ENG)“Thank you for contacting us regarding the outcome of the facial verification process. After verification by our Customer Support following your contestation of the decision, we regret to confirm that you have not satisfactorily passed the facial verification process. In accordance with article 13.5 of our General Conditions of Use, your account is blocked”._ 

_(FR) “Nous vous remercions de nous avoir contactés au sujet du résultat de la procédure de vérification faciale. Après vérification par notre Service Qualité suite à votre contestation de la décision, nous avons le regret de vous confirmer que vous n’avez pas réussi de manière adéquate la procédure de vérification faciale. Hello,

Here is the feedback from Deloitte on it. Long story short, it does not seem to be connected with our TOMS dispute but we should make sure that the answers we give are consistent of what we are saying in the TOMS proceedings.

There is also the topic of GDPR which they refer to and with which the Privacy team can hopefully assist with.

Here is the reply:

We have reviewed the letter and HMRC’s informal information request and set out our observations below, we note that we have not reviewed the request in the light of Bolt’s GDPR obligations.

Regarding the information requested, Bolt may wish to provide the information to HMRC and is permitted to do so under Clause 4 of the +Privacy Notice: Drivers+ which are incorporated into the Driver Terms & Conditions dated 25 April 2023, which provides that Bolt will “only share when there is a proper reason to do so”.

When HMRC ordinarily requests information from a taxpayer, they do so using their formal information powers captured in Schedule 36 of the Finance Act 2008 (“*Schedule 36*”).  Under these powers, HMRC is permitted to issue notices to third parties legally requiring them to provide information and documents to HMRC about a taxpayer.  However, Schedule 36 provides that if HMRC issue such a notice to Bolt, that HMRC must obtain the taxpayer (driver’s consent) or obtain approval from the Tribunal in order to obtain the information. In this letter we note that HMRC have specifically asked Bolt not to disclose that it is providing this information to HMRC about the driver, implying that driver consent has not been obtained.  

Bolt therefore could ask that HMRC request the information formally under their Schedule 36 information powers.  However, this will be a commercial decision for Bolt to take given that there is no prohibition per the driver terms to provide this information per se. However, we note that we have not validated whether for GDPR reasons Bolt would need a more formal document to provide the information.  

Although the questions look broadly straightforward, however, there are several questions we noted which should be consistent with what Bolt has told HMRC as regards the TOMS litigation (and the worker status litigation):

* Questions 3 -5 & 16: the employment status of the driver;
* Question 7: We are unsure how this relates to the driver in question as it appear to provide information on how Bolt determines a driver’s commission;
* Question 12 – 14: This does not appear to be information Bolt would have available.

Please let us know whether you have any questions regarding the above or would benefit from a call.

Hey [~accountid:604aad641f946f00699d88d1],

thanks for letting us know about this.

1. When we launch a feature for employees only, we still should comply with the privacy law and inform them about how the feature works and how we process their personal data. Sure, we should not report that any bug report can be visible in a slack channel, etc., since it’s details about where and how we see bug reports.
2. However, the way this Slack channel works should be adjusted. Bolt and other data controllers should have appropriate data security in place and one of these is access control to personal data. In our case, the channel should not be a public channel, only people who need to work with the reports should be in the channel. Channel should be private. 
3. For these cases, we treat our employees as Bolt Food users rather than employees. We treat them as employees if we process their personal data in the context of employment relationship. Other relationship, any AB tests on employees, should be considered as test on users, but we just understand that these people will work closely with us to improve our services. However, in case of any data incident, they are entitled to full protection under the privacy law.


*To sum up:*
1. In this case, we will document this incident, but I don’t see that we should report it to authorities as it seems no risk for the user (employee). *Please advise whether this employee received any negative feedback or was discriminated for this situation?* 
2. Please adjust the access controls in this channel so only people who need to know the bug reports for their work (fix bugs, proceed with support tickets, etc) have access to it. Not all Bolt employees should access this.
3. Please note that if we launch any tests of feature for employees only, we should comply with the privacy law: have a legal basis to process their data, inform them about the way we process the data, if we share this data with other third parties (our providers, SDKs, etc.). In this case, before launching any feature to them, the team should raise a ticket to our team to assess this.

*SQL to replicate table above*

{code:sql}WITH event_table AS (
SELECT
eventname,
eventprops_campaign_name,
eventprops_campaign_type,
CASE WHEN eventname IN ('Notification Sent','Control Group')  THEN eventprops_campaign_id ELSE SPLIT_PART(eventprops_wzrk_id,'_', 1) END message_id,
CASE WHEN eventname IN ('Notification Sent','Control Group') THEN eventdate  ELSE DATE_PARSE(SPLIT_PART(eventprops_wzrk_id,'_', 2), '%Y%m%d') END sent_dt,
profile_identity,
CAST(parse_datetime(CAST(ts AS varchar), 'yyyyMMddHHmmss') AS timestamp) AS timestamp,
eventdate
FROM ng_clevertap.driver_events AS events 
WHERE
eventname IN ('Notification Sent', 'Notification Viewed', 'Notification Clicked','Control Group')
AND eventdate BETWEEN DATE(DATE_ADD('MONTH', -12, DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', CURRENT_DATE))) AND CURRENT_DATE)
SELECT
date_trunc('month', eventdate) AS eventmonth,
event_table.message_id,
event_table.eventprops_campaign_name AS campaign_name,
event_table.eventprops_campaign_type AS campaign_type,
COUNT(DISTINCT event_table.message_id || CAST(event_table.timestamp AS VARCHAR) || event_table.profile_identity) AS count_event_with_null_channel
FROM event_table
--LEFT JOIN ng_clevertap.driver_message_properties_latest AS prop ON event_table.message_id = CAST(prop.message_id AS VARCHAR)
LEFT JOIN ng_public.etl_clevertap_driver_campaign_journey_properties AS prop ON event_table.message_id = CAST(prop.message_id AS VARCHAR)
WHERE eventdate BETWEEN date '2023-07-01' AND date '2023-07-31'
AND eventname = 'Notification Sent'
AND prop.channel IS NULL
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 5 DESC LIMIT 20{code}

I'd like to inform you that the updates to the ZAF Annual Vacation system are now in production.

Previously, our time-off plan followed the calendar year, running from January to December, with a carryover period of 6 months, also aligned with the calendar year. 

However, this arrangement did not comply with the carryover regulations mandated in South Africa. In South Africa, employees are required to have a carryover period determined by their anniversary date. As you may recall, previously, everyone's carryover would expire in July, irrespective of their anniversary date.

Now, your annual leave balances have been adjusted to conform with South African local laws. This transition involves changing from a "calendar year" to an "anniversary year" format. With this change, your balances were recalculated based on your anniversary period. 

In your case, your anniversary period is from February 1st to January 31st and then add 6 months of carryover. Your carryover expires on August 1st then.

The difference with the old plan is 8,12 days, so as per approval from Simphiwe, I added these days to your balance. (_In your old plan you had 16,41 days by the end of the period and in the updated one is 8,12 days. This difference is caused by the new carryover rule based on the anniversary period_).

Regarding our liability, retaining the original wording means that we would be liable for any direct AND any indirect damage caused to the leased premises by us, our people and/or any other people that we grant access. This means e.g. that if we break a wall, we would be liable for not only replacing the wall/reimbursing the landlord for replacing it, but also for any loss of profit, loss of income etc. that the landlord suffers as a consequence of this damage (i.e. indirect damages or consequential damages). It's not ideal and goes against Bolt's global contracting principles.

On another note, our liability under this clause is inherently a little less risky than under the indemnity clauses (where the landlord has accepted to limit our liability to direct damages). 

In my opinion, we can accept to let this go from a legal perspective, but it is still up to business to decide whether we can accept the financial risk from a commercial perspective.

Hi [~accountid:6333d09c07a27ebeff16855f]

So unfortunately in Stebby only a certain types of massages are compensated. To qualify, the service provider must be a rehabilitation physician, physiotherapist, activity therapist, speech therapist or clinical psychologist registered in the Health Administration Information System, who provides their professional services. The tax incentive does not apply if the service provider holds another professional certificate (for example, a massage therapist, lymph therapist, masseur, chiropractor, and so on). So unfortunately, a masseur does not qualify. 

If you're not sure if the service you want is compensated, it's always best to buy through Stebby since the platform will let you know if the service you want is compensated and you can add that as a filter when searching for services. Or you can just use that as an indicator if a similar service from a non-stebby provider will be accepted. 

You could also consider switching to Confido health insurance since it also has a category for rehabilitation (with physicians referral) and some types of massages could be covered by that. 

You can read about confido on our Confluence page: https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BILP/pages/3165650957/Confido+Health+Insurance

** Do we need one set of access credentials or do we need them for each VAT code? If per each VAT code, who is doing registration on tax auth side?
*** Maret is researching
** In the example invoice there is customer mobile. Currently we do not get it from billing document.
** What is their API's average response time?
** What is the load from our side, how many invoices per day/per month we would have?

** By what value are duplicates avoided?

(As there are notes in the bottom of Sample receipt, I am afraid that Bolt has to put together the invoice. This is responsibility of billing document team.)
If we have to put together PDF receipt, then we need to get following data:
*** Taxpayer details: VRN, Serial Number, UIN and Tax Office
*** We need to double-check if discount amount are sent for TZ invoices from billing document.
*** What is CNO on Sample receipt?
*** What is receipt verification code? Maybe we get it back from the response?
** Questions about XML payload:
*** EFDSERIAL - it is number assigned to the virtual device. How can we get this value? (A: This information will be provided by TRA)
*** MOBILENUM - is it mandatory field and how do we get it from billing doc.
*** RCTNUM - as it has to be only digits, then our uuid is not suitable for it. But sharing our invoice id would expose business size.
*** DC- daiy counter. How can we calculate and store this number as we receive invoices per drivers/fleets in not-guaranteed order). 
*** RCTVNUM - where do we get this invoice verification number?
*** Question about Item collection
**** Item ID - billing document does not have this value. Is it number field or can we generate hash from item description?
*** Discounts - lets doublecheck if we get them for TZ from billing document
*** Questions about PAYMENTS section
**** Do we get PMTTYPE payment method type data from billing document? I am afraid that not fully (e.g EMONEY, etc)
*** How is EFDMSSIGNATURE value put together?
*** Do we need to submit also Z reports, which are summaries of sales for the day?
**** In Z report there is TICKETSVOID which means “Total number of tickets voided/cancelled in the system and therefore not sent to TRA” - probably those even do not reach fiscalization system. Also there is a requirement “If transaction is cancelled, next transaction should take not reuse transaction of cancelled transaction it should take new number in the sequence“.
*** How long is a token valid? In document it is written that the token period is in seconds, but not specified how many seconds.
*** There is separate QR code url. Do we need to separately go to that url and get the QR code (and then store for billing doc to put together the PDF)

* Sending the invoices in order is important. 
* Dealing with registrations and tokens will make fiscalization integration much more difficult than with Ghana.
* Also there comes addtional complexity with storing cert key and token securely.

Nevertheless, we still need to be transparent about the amendment. 
* *Accepted - Bolt’s liability for any damage to the lease object (clause 21.1).* We have accepted the landlord’s pushback to retain the original wording in clause 21.1, entailing liability for any direct _and_ _indirect_ damage arising due to our negligence/wilful misconduct by us, or our staff, contractors, etc. and others to whom we grant access. Nevertheless, our liability is more limited under this clause than under the indemnity clauses (where the landlord has accepted to limit our liability to direct damages). The landlord would have to prove damages and, for indirect damages, causal link - which is often very difficult. Although it is important to know what insurances we have and what they cover in Norway (e.g., in Finland, our liability insurance covers our computers as well), this does not change our assessment regarding the liability-clause 21.1 (see above).

As requested by Julien, I had a look at this in Michela’s absence. In fact, [~accountid:62bff85c118b20bee2bdca35] had already started reviewing this and we briefly exchanged on this as well. Here are our thoughts:

* Premium / Berline category already exists in FR but you want to now offer it only to certain drivers.
* *What will you do about the existing drivers in this category?* Will you automatically remove them? I suggest that we at least send them an email explaining that this category is being terminated, however we will offer a new similar category to drivers who have [completed X number of rides on the Bolt platform and have X category of vehicles etc].
* For this new category, *what do you want to put in place as ‘eligibility criteria’?* 
** *_minimum number of rides:_* 
*** sounds ok but keen to get an idea of what sport of number you’re thinking about? 
*** Also, do you know if Uber is making this visible, ie everybody can see that to be on their Premium Category you need to have at least X number of rides on the Uber platform? 
*** In any case, this is not something that I have seen in Uber jurisprudence, so I’m not too worried - that doesn’t mean though that it wouldn’t be retained against a platform as I assume a FR court could say it is part of a Power of Management and Monitoring the Driver’s Activity, which are seen by FR courts as an indication that there is a subordination link and therefore an employment relationship.
** *_“driver score”_*: what are you referring to here? Do you mean instead the _average rating that a driver gets from passengers_? If that’s the case, it comes from the passengers so it is neutral from Bolt’s perspective and therefore it should be fine (*_FYI_* a FR court held against one of our competitors that the fact that passengers are invited to rate the driver's performance coupled with the fact that the platform can deactivate access if the rating falls below a minimum average rating set unilaterally by the platform means that the platform is monitoring the driver’s activity and therefore he should be reclassified as an employee - however we wouldn’t go that far here - we would just favour drivers with a better rate).
** *_car requirements_* (6 years old max, between 4 and 9 seats, at least 4 doors, power rating of 84 kW or more): this is perfect as these are _objectives criteria_ which have nothing to do with the driver himself.
** *_anything else?_*
* *Imposing soft behavioural requirements*: [~accountid:62bff85c118b20bee2bdca35] and I agree that +we should+ +*not*+ +do this+. We would recommend to not even mention this or encourage drivers to do this. As explained by Michela, this would materially increase our reclassification risks (as this would be seen by FR courts as the exercise of a power of direction, which could corroborate the existence of a subordination link and hence resulting into reclassification of the driver).

Hi Antonio, I would like to make a summary of the matter and feedback:

*GENERAL LEGAL RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH DRIVER BLOCKING*

* Blocking drivers might be seen as fulfilling criteria 2, 3, 4 and/or 5 of the ATD Law. While it seems very difficult not to control or supervise the activity of the drivers, our outside attorney advice was the following: the only way to avoid meeting those criteria is to go through the fleet and say to the fleet that a client complained about a driver so can the fleet please do something to address this issue. If the fleet doesn't do anything, the outside attorney advised that Bolt should envisage imposing a penalty first (to the fleet), and then could potentially block the fleet (not the driver) after a few events if the fleet hasn’t done anything. Disabling the driver if the fleet doesn't do it would be very risky. Based on this, *any blocking done by Bolt directly on the driver is a risk*. This is something where we are all aligned I believe.
* Below, we’re highlighting the *mitigation measures* from reclassification point of view in relation to driver blocking, starting with the strongest ones (the ones that would really help us defend ourselves in a reclassification claim) and moving down to the alternative scenarios in case the previous ones are not possible/envisageable to implement in the short term (as we understand is the case):
** *Putting in place processes allowing the fleet to block its drivers who are in breach of T&Cs, after this has been flagged by Bolt to the fleet* (in accordance with our T&Cs) - _this is the best legal solution, considering we only have an agreement with fleets and this would mean we are not at risk of meeting any ATD criteria._
** *Blocking the entire fleet in case one of its drivers is in breach of T&Cs*. _We would recommend at least to look into putting in place a process allowing us to block fleets when several of their drivers are in breach. E.g. if a fleets receives safety events on more than 50% of their drivers._
** If none of the first 2 options are developed, then it means Bolt is at risk of meeting several reclassification criteria - however, from an experience perspective, *properly informing the driver and its fleet* means that potentially we create less situations where drivers are unhappy and therefore we decrease the risks of drivers willing to sue us for reclassification - however ACT can always initiate claims and then a court would review all the facts, so such approach re: blocking might be held against us and be ruled by a court as fulfilling several criteria. In such case, we recommend that *Legal to review comms to drivers and fleets*.

*REVIEW OF THE FRAUD COMMUNICATION*

{code:sql}with base as (
select
	b.country_code
	, a.client_rating_comment 
	, case when regexp_like(a.client_rating_comment, '(?i)kissing|crash|smoking') then 1 else 0 end
											as comment_has_safety_keyword
from glue.ng_public.company_order_try_local 			as a
left join ng_public.admin_system_city  				as b
	on a.city_id = b.id  
where 1=1
	and a.client_rating_comment is not null
	and a.client_rating = 1
	and a.created_date >= date('2023-08-01')
	and a.created_date < date('2023-09-01')
)
select 
	country_code
	, count(client_rating_comment) 				as comment_count
from base 
where comment_has_safety_keyword = 1
group by 1{code}

* *DAC7 Law:* 10 years. Article 14(2) Law n 36/2023 of 26 July determines the following: "The records referred to in the previous paragraph must be available for a period of 10 years from the end of the reporting period to which they relate."

I now understand that the user actually abandoned the scooter in a “no parking zone”. Therefore, from a legal perspective, my assessment is that the user has no additional rights to compensation. The user may also choose to end the contract with Bolt. Please see further details below.

*Bolt’s right to charge the user for the whole trip (60 minutes)*

From a legal perspective, the user was still renting the scooter while the scooter was in the red zone, given that parking is not permitted in red zones. Therefore, we are legally entitled to charge the user for the whole renting time, in this case: 60 minutes since the trip was not ended earlier (properly in accordance with Bolt’s T&Cs, including any instructions in the app, all of which the user has agreed to follow upon unlocking the scooter). 

In light of the above, we are not legally obliged to refund the user for any part of the 60 minutes' trip. The user may choose to accept our refund in Bolt Balance, but if the user chooses not to, we are not legally obliged to offer anything else as compensation. Nevertheless, I understand that we do offer refunds even though the user may not necessarily be _legally_ entitled to it. Any such refund would be a commercial decision rather than a legal one. 

*The user’s request to withdraw from the contract*

Regarding the user’s request to withdraw from the contract with Bolt, the user is free to _end the contract_ with us. However, for rentals, as a rule, users have no right to “withdraw” from the contract with Bolt, except for in relation to pre-paid passes that have not yet been activated. Given that the user has not purchased any pre-paid pass, ending the contract in this case would basically mean deleting the app / stop using our services. 

If the user decides to end the contract with us, any balance left on Bolt Balance due to our refund is automatically deleted according to our T&Cs for Bolt Balance. We are not legally obliged to refund the user in cash instead if the contract is ended.

In addition, according to our T&Cs, the user can be charged with a parking fee of 60 SEK if the user abandoned the vehicle in a no-parking zone (and a red zone is, from what I understand, a no-parking zone). 

Please let me know if you have any further questions on the legal aspects of this issue, or if we can close the ticket.

Best regards,

Ida

Tested the following scenarios on iOS and Android devices (iPhone 12 Pro (15.1.1), iPhone 6S (15.4.1), Huawei P30 Pro (10), Google Pixel (10)) using feature build 1.50 (1705404):

# Smart categories are displayed in the dish carousel when their position is less than 0.
# When the config is set to "render_in": "tile-carousel" for a smart category, it will be displayed in the tile carousel.
# When the config is set to "render_in": "dish-carousel" for a smart category, it will still be displayed in the tile carousel.
# When the config is set to "render_in": "tile-grid" for a smart category, it will still be displayed in the tile grid.
# When a category is not active, adding the config won't affect the app, and the category still won't be displayed.
# Making a category inactive will remove it from grid layout or dish or tile carousels.
# By changing the render in config the category will show in correct place and won’t show in other places. for example if the config is tile-carousel, the category won’t show in grid layout or dish carousel
# Categories are ordered based on the position number in the tile carousel.
# When the config is set to "render_in": "tile-carousel" but position is less than 0, the category will be displayed in the tile carousel, with its position number defining its place (ordering will start from the smallest number).
# The UI was tested in both light and dark modes.
# When the number of categories is more than 3 in tile carousel it will scroll horizontally
# When the number of categories in tile carousel decreases to 3, the scroll will remove
# By disabling the tile layout FF, all categories will be shown in the dish carousel, regardless of their config in the admin panel.
# By changing the dynamic config for the 'save me' category, it's possible to display it in either the tile carousel or dish carousel as well as grid layout
# Order of categories in search and category view is the same as menu screen

The user seems to have parked the scooter in an area where parking is not permitted, and therefore, the user is liable to pay the parking fine issued by Stockholm stad to us and forwarded by us to the user. Please see further details below.

*Users' liability for non-compliant parking*

_The user’s liability to Bolt for any parking of an e-vehicle_, which the user has rented via the Bolt app, in a way or place that is not in accordance with the rules following from our T&Cs, including any instructions in the app, and any applicable laws and regulations, etc. (referred to in the following as “*non-compliant parking*”) is regulated by our T&Cs for E-vehicles. The T&Cs state that by unlocking an e-vehicle, the user accepts liability to pay any fines, fees, etc. issued (to Bolt or to the user directly) due to any non-compliant parking.

In light of this and based on the information you have provided in the ticket, my assessment from a legal perspective is that the user is liable for the non-compliant parking in this case. Thus, Bolt has a right to forward the fine imposed by Stockholm stad to the user and the user is obligated to pay the fine. Nevertheless, Bolt must have sufficient proof showing (i) the non-compliant parking, and (ii) the basis for our claim against the user, i.e. the parking fine issued by Stockholm stad. Please see more information on this as well as some questions below.

*Proof of the user’s liability for the parking fine*

In order to claim payment of the fine from the user, Bolt must be able to prove that the e-vehicle in question was wrongfully parked by the user and that this resulted in a fine from Stockholm stad. 

_Proof to support the non-compliant parking_

From what I understand, we know that the user parked the scooter at a spot where parking is not permitted according to our T&Cs. Please confirm whether we have proof to show this, and what the proof consists of. 

_Proof to support our right to claim payment for the parking fine from the user_

I understand that Stockholm stad issued the document attached by you in this ticket to support Stockholm stad’s claim for the parking fine against Bolt. We have then forwarded the claim onto the user, as we are entitle to do according to the T&Cs. If we consider the documentation provided by Stockholm stad as insufficient proof of our liability for the parking fine, we needs to request further information from Stockholm stad to support this. * Is the attached document the only proof of the wrongful parking that we have received from Stockholm stad? 
* Does the documentation that we receive from Stockholm stad in connection with parking fines usually contain any additional pages with stamps, signatures, or similar, that prove to us that the document is indeed issued by Stockholm stad? I am only asking to see whether we have any additional information to show the user that this document is indeed an official document issued by Stockholm stad.

Also, I wanted to let you know that we made changes to the annual leave plan.

Previously, our time-off plan followed the calendar year, running from January to December, with a carryover period of 6 months, also aligned with the calendar year. 

However, this arrangement did not comply with the carryover regulations mandated in South Africa. In South Africa, employees are required to have a carryover period determined by their anniversary date. As you may recall, previously, everyone's carryover would expire in July, irrespective of their anniversary date.

Now, your annual leave balances have been adjusted to conform with South African local laws. This transition involves changing from a "calendar year" to an "anniversary year" format. With this change, your balances were recalculated based on your anniversary period. 

In your case, your anniversary period is from June 1st (as you were hired in June) and it lasts till June next year and then add 6 months of carryover. Your carryover expires on December 1st.

Kind Regards,

+*Things to flag*+

* The matters I would highlight are: Bolt must be aware that the repairing obligation puts a positive obligation on Bolt to pay for any damage that is made to the *Office Space* as well as the *premises* (the building the office is in). Ideally we would want to narrow this down, so Bolt to only be responsible for any damage caused by Bolt to the Office Space (the room Bolt are occupying) as opposed to the Premises (the whole property). This is because Bolt does not want to be in a situation, where if anything happens to the Premises, which was not the fault of Bolt, Bolt end up responsible for paying damages. *Option 2:* You can proceed at risk, taking into consideration that this is an unmanned office, however you will have to be aware that even though it is an unmanned office Bolt could potentially become liable to damage in the premises.

We covered some of the same problems with [~accountid:6345aaf2db32d9ce175cc1c9] and others in the delivery data modelling workshop.

We agreed on the following principles:

* We will create separate duration tables for order and courier/driver
* Granularity = 15 min
* Order durations will serve the purpose of understanding the durations per order and for summing up the total durations as they would be without any batching/overlaps
* Courier/driver durations will serve the purpose of understanding courier/driver time spend, they will not double count time if multiple orders are being worked on at the same time
* For the courier/driver durations, we will split up the different TYPES of activity, but we will not distinguish the number of orders currently being worked on. 

Sample state log:

||*courier_id/driver_id*||*order_id*||*to_state*||*timestamp*||

|123|1|picked_up_order|10:05|
|123|2|accepted_order|10:10|
|123|2|picked_up_order|10:15|
|123|1|delivered_order|10:20|
|123|3|accepted_order|10:25|
|123|2|delivered_order|10:30|
|123|3|picked_up_order|10:35|
|123|3|delivered_order|10:40|

Sample order durations:

||*courier_id/driver_id*||*order_id*||*time_window*||*state*||*duration (min)*||
|123|1|10:00|accepted_order|5|
|123|1|10:00|picked_up_order|10|
|123|1|10:15|picked_up_order|5|

|123|3|10:15|accepted_order|5|
|123|3|10:30|accepted_order|5|
|123|3|10:30|picked_up_order|5|

Sample courier order durations (can we somehow use the order durations to create this table for courier durations? no, because the minutes may or may not be from overlapped time frames, durations are not accurate enough to tell us):

has_accepted_orders__no_picked_up_orders

no_accepted_orders__has_picked_up_orders

* Article 14 of *Cyber Crime Law* determines the following obligations: _1 - If, in the course of the proceedings, it becomes necessary for the production of evidence, with a view to discovering the truth, to obtain specific and determined computer data stored in a given computer system, the competent judicial authority shall order whoever has availability or control of that data to communicate it to the proceedings or to allow access to it, under penalty of punishment for disobedience. 2 - The order referred to in the previous paragraph shall identify the data in question. 3 - In compliance with the order described in paragraphs 1 and 2, whoever has availability or control of such data shall communicate it to the competent judicial authority or allow access to the computer system where it is stored, under penalty of disobedience. 4 - The provisions of this article shall apply to service providers, who may be ordered to communicate data relating to their customers or subscribers to the procedure, including any information other than traffic or content data, contained in the form of computer data or in any other form, held by the service provider, and which makes it possible to determine: a) The type of communication service used, the technical measures taken in this regard and the period of service; (b) the identity, postal or geographical address and telephone number of the subscriber, and any other access number, billing and payment data available on the basis of a contract or service agreement; or (c) any other information on the location of the communication equipment, available on the basis of a contract or service agreement._

* Staying current with the latest version ensures compliance with industry standards and builds trust with users and partners alike.

 WITH child_case AS (
 SELECT

        ,support_case_id                                                           AS parent_case_id
        ,cast(get_json_object(event_data, '$.support_case_id') AS bigint)          AS child_case_id
        , row_number() OVER (partition by cast(get_json_object(event_data, '$.support_case_id') AS bigint) ORDER BY created DESC)   AS rw_nr
    FROM customer_support.support_case_event

       ,child_case_id
    FROM child_case
    WHERE rw_nr = 1
)

Hi [~accountid:5b8d306bfa38ae2c89608b95] , please see below Malta regulatory framework related with (e-)cigarettes:

* *Can (e-)cigarettes be sold online?* Yes. There is no provision or regulation that prohibits the sale of e-cigarettes simply because they are sold online. The restrictions applicable make no distinction between online or offline sale. Smokeless Tobacco Products are banned completely and cannot be supplied in any way.
* *Are there age restrictions?* On E-Cigarettes insofar as they contain tobacco: 
18 years. Tobacco (Smoking Control) Act provides that no person shall sell, supply or distribute by way of compensation or otherwise, any cigarettes, cigars, tobacco, tobacco products or smoking requisites to any person who is under the age of eighteen years, or in any manner induce such person to smoke.
* *Does anyone requires a licence?* 
** Bolt: No specific type code applies under S.L. 441.07 for platforms; 
** Vendor: Depending on the nature of the vendor, some commercial activities require a licence under the Code of Police Laws, and others are exempt under S.L. 441.07. 
** Courier: no licence requirement under Type Code 64.1 of S.L. 441.07
* *Who must verify ID?* The law does not technically oblige user ID verification but age verification which can in turn be best verified using an official document such as ID, Licence, Passport etc.
* *Does the user ID need to be verified for each time the order contains age-restricted items?* 
** The law does not specify this granular detail however, if the age is verified at account creation, we would argue that is enough. We have not traced any case-law or specific instances where this has been interpreted in the online, virtual environment. 
** A number of Maltese online shops and supermarkets selling alcohol have only implemented user self verification requiring the user to fill in a date of birth or tick a check box.
** No penalty for not checking ID per se, but there is a fine for the supply of alcohol to minors: a fine up to EUR 1,164.69 on a first conviction.
* *How should Bolt verify age?* The safest option from a probative value point of view is for BOLT CS to verify some form of identification document on account creation.

Hi, [~accountid:61c2f85f90cfd20071570ff8]! Thank you for reaching out. This seems to be a though case. I would explain to their lawyer why wording that they proposed will not work in this situation and what Bolt tries to achieve as we are not really able to compromise here. Therefore I prepared a detailed explanation that will hopefully help and provide some relief. You can share my explanation with them.

Point 3.7 is one of Bolt’s hard requirements that we cannot just drop or compromise. This is because we want to ensure that we provide the best experience both to Users and any persons providing services such as drivers. Bolt should have a proper recourse in cases where a User for some reason did not pay for their ride or rental in case such ride or rental was part of Bolt Business rides/rentals and if a User caused any damage while using Bolt services as part of Bolt Business.

This was the proposed wording: 
”Customer agrees to indemnify any cost or damage to Bolt or to any other person that results from {color:#ff5630}breach of Obligations regulated by this Agreement by{color} User {color:#ff5630}or Customer{color} {color:#ff5630}-using the Bolt Services-{color}  or violating the applicable law. Customer authorises Bolt to charge such damage {color:#ff5630}-cost-{color} using Customer’s elected payment method. {color:#ff5630}Bolt shall provide documented evidence of such breach, including the proven amount of damages, without undue delay upon Customer's request. For the avoidance of doubt, it does not cover damage caused to a third party, in particular the carrier, driver, courier or any other independent user of the Bolt Services{color}”

# Adding wording “breach of Obligations regulated by this Agreement by“ - this clause is targeting Users only in terms of their violations and they are not parties to this Agreement. Their obligations are set out in Terms and Conditions for Passengers. Also, Bolt is concerned not only with their breach of obligations, but also any damage to the property or persons while using Bolt Services, so the proposed wording is not suitable for this purpose.
# Adding wording “or Customer” - we do not want to extend this clause to the Customer as the Customer will not be using Bolt Services. Customer benefits only from Bolt Business and Users are those who will use Bolt Services that are facilitated by Bolt Business service that Bolt provides to the Customer.
# Deleting wording “using the Bolt Services” - this wording is needed to specify that Bolt is concerned only about problems associated with the use of Bolt Services. 
# Substituting word “cost” with “damage” - the word cost is used to limit the ability of Bolt to charge the Customer only costs that are associated with the Users use of Bolt Services. Such costs would normally be cost of an unpaid ride or rental if it occurred as part of Bolt Business programme. Any damages would be claimed following the proper procedures for claiming damages as it would be unusual if Bolt would be able to automatically charge Customer for any damages. Therefore, this substitution is not in favour of the Customer.
# Adding wording “Bolt shall provide documented evidence of such breach, including the proven amount of damages, without undue delay upon Customer's request.“ - we agree that the Customer has the right to request information about any additional costs that are charged as a result of using Bolt Services by the User. We would suggest using “Bolt shall provide documented evidence of such cost upon Customer request.“ to specify that we will provide evidence of costs that are charged automatically. We do not need to tailor this clause to take into account damages because damages will not be claimed automatically. Bolt will need to present the case explaining that there were any damages and provide all relevant evidence to be able to claim damages. Such claims would be handled as an ordinary litigation which would include pre-litigation stage where parties will try to resolve any issues amicably, but if this will not be possible, then Bolt will have the right claim any damages from the Customer in the court and Bolt will need to prove to the court that Bolt’s claim is legitimate.
# Adding wording “For the avoidance of doubt, it does not cover damage caused to a third party, in particular the carrier, driver, courier or any other independent user of the Bolt Services“ - this is implied by this clause in case Bolt can prove to the Customer or the court that the claim is legitimate. As the Bolt Services are utilised by Users in the interests of the Customer, and Users are added/removed by the Customer then it’s only natural that Customer is also obliged to indemnify any damage or other exceptional cost caused by the User during its use of Bolt Services. Therefore, we are not able to add this wording.

Our final proposed wording would be this:

_Customer agrees to indemnify any cost or damage to Bolt or to any other person that results from User using the Bolt Services or violating the applicable law. Customer authorises Bolt to charge such cost using Customer’s elected payment method._ {color:#ff5630}_Bolt shall provide documented evidence of such cost upon Customer request._{color}

I hope these detailed explanations will help.

From a Privacy/Technical and Organisational Security Measures point of view, and to build on [~accountid:624407b68678e900705a1a5d]'s recommendations below:

* Create a Document indicating that Criselda Sindana, Mohale Hlahatsi and Shabnam Banu Badroodien are the personnel authorised to access the room and the CCTV footage;
* Ensure that the access control system is set up to restrict access to any other personnel.
* Ensure that no third-parties (like Drivers/Riders/other employees) visit the room - so, if someone is looking for something that they have lost, rather take a description of it, go look for it, and bring it back to them. On this note I recommend that you create a register to capture these kinds of lost and found transactions and keep that register in safe place, like a locked cabinet.
* Ensure the authorised personnel always lock the door to the room when leaving and close it behind them when inside.
* Carefully manage the handling of ID books/phones by verifying who the owner is and confirming that they are who they say they are — *sharing someone’s ID with a person who is not authorised to hold that ID would be considered a personal data breach* – log these transactions as above.
* Don’t leave any IDs, papers, or any other documents with personal data contained in them lying around - they should be locked in a safe within the room and only certain personnel should have access to that safe’s code. *Unauthorised sight of documents intended for filing with personal data on them would also constitute a personal data breach*.
* Access to the CCTV footage should also be password protected. Store that password in a secure manner.

The filter logic is that updates will only be ingested if {{data}} is not null. New inserts will always be ingested, so that’s why the table still has data.

However, this also means that the table really can’t be backfilled, because for existing records there is no information if this record has been updated or not. So assuming that the filter for the existing ingestion was applied for a good reason, a backfill would create inconsistent data within the table.

[~accountid:61b9ad769666c0006f83453a] there are two approaches now:

* Talk to stakeholders, and hope that someone can remember why this filter was applied. Maybe the reason why the filter was originally applied is not valid anymore, and we can ignore it for the backfill.
* If nobody can remember, setup a new ingestion for the table, without the filter, to a new table. This would solve the backfill problem, and stakeholders can investigate the differences between the old and the new table to figure out what problem the filter logic solved before.

# Clause 2.5 - Bolt provides the list of actions that it considers unacceptable in clauses 2.5.1, 2.5.2, 2.5.3, 2.5.4, 2.5.5 and 2.5.6. Some of the actions mentioned in these clauses are broader than others, but the aim of Bolt is to protect itself from situations where previously unknown activity will take place that can harm Bolt. Provisions of clause 2.5 are industry standard provisions in relation to services that are provided using any kind of software, but there are also additional provisions specific to the services that Bolt provides. Bolt does not think that it is possible to introduce more specific provisions and sees no need in doing so.
# Clause 3.2 - Clause 3.2 is one of Bolt’s hard requirements that we cannot just drop or compromise. This is because we want to ensure that we provide the best experience both to Users and any persons providing services such as drivers. Bolt should have a proper recourse in cases where the User for some reason did not pay for their ride or rental in case such ride or rental was part of Bolt Business rides/rentals and if the User caused any damage while using Bolt services as part of Bolt Business. 
# Clause 6.3 - Loss of personal data is treated separately. Clause 6.3.2 relates only to loss of general data that could be uploaded to Bolt systems and gets lost. We do not think that the risk is real, but we would still like to keep our terms standard. Such loss of data does not exclude Bolt responsibilities under data protection law as this exclusion is in no way connected to that responsibility.Please clarify to which comment the second point makes reference.
# Clause 6.4 - Customer is responsible for its representatives, e.g Business Portal administrators, or Users unauthorised, fraudulent or other unlawful activity, e.g should a Portal administrator (knowingly or by mistake) add unentitled Users to Customers Team Account. Despite Customer not being the contracting party under the Terms of Service the Customer remains liable for all the damage caused by its Users from their usage of Bolt Services (i.e Bolt considers the User and the Customer as solidary obligors). Bolt limits its claims only to the actual damages suffered, and enables the Customer to object to any deduction.
# Clause 7.3 - The clause allows the party to terminate the Agreement in case of a material breach of the Agreement. If the proposed changes are accepted this clause will provide the parties with the same rights as described in clause 7.2. The benefit of such change is questionable because 7 days will not give much more protection. The original clause is a common clause that allows parties to terminate an agreement without prior notice in case there is a material breach and such material breach is not always specified because it might be hard to predict such material breach apart from the most obvious ones such as non-payment and harm to the other party’s reputation. It may happen that the breach will be so serious that waiting 7 days may significantly increase the damage resulting from such breach. We therefore do not think that this change is necessary considering the nature of the contractual relationship and services to be provided in this particular case.
# Clause 7.5 - Bolt cannot remove this clause as this is absolutely vital protection for Bolt. However, Bolt will still be able to assist with any urgent matters if such issues are raised via Support function and do not jeopardise investigation of the issue.
# Clause 8.5 - notice to the other party means a notice given in accordance with the provisions of clause 8.1 to the other party to the Agreement.

Switching between different schemas can potentially create at least following cases when balance or obligations will not be reflected in a correct way

h2. Examples:

# *FROM net (1 account) TO “2 accounts”*

* initial state 
** Main (food) balance -100
* switch to “2 account” happens: 
** Main -100 
** Credit 0
* payment received: 100 (goes to credit) 
* food orders: 50 (goes to main “food” account)
* resulting state is:  
** Main: -50
** Credit +100

*Problem*: no payout (=main account is <=0). Although the payout for food orders (50) should be generated

*Current approach:* Food covers previous debt first, fees are accumulated on another account. 

*Another approach:* transfer amounts depending on sign to a relevant balance at time of switch - create additional transaction. For example,

* transfer -100 from main to Credit, 
* then payment will compensate debt on credit account and food will go to main 
** Main:50
** Credit:0
* there will be a payout of 50 as result of food orders generated

# FROM “2 accounts” To “Net” (1 account)

* initial state 
** Main (food): 0 
** Credit -100
* switch to “gross” happens. If credit account is not “closed” and no transfers between accounts then: 
** Main 0 
** Credit -100
* payment: 100 
* food orders: 50
* resulting state 
** Main: 150 
** Credit: -100

 *Problem* - There will be payout of 150 and still debt on -100 on Credit account

*Example:* [https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/delivery/providers/17221?tab=info|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/delivery/providers/17221?tab=info]

*Solution:* if not in “two account” mode - then first cover with a payment negative credit balance (if exists) and rest of the amount to main (food) account.

The cause of slow fleet MySQL response and failed connections is high concurrency requests to the MySQL instance.

[https://monitor.boltint.net/d/000000036/proxysql-overview?orgId=1&from=1695130624000&to=1695132436000|https://monitor.boltint.net/d/000000036/proxysql-overview?orgId=1&from=1695130624000&to=1695132436000]

According to [pmm.sqldb|http://pmm2.sqldb/graph/d/mysql-innodb/mysql-innodb-details?orgId=1&from=1695131226289&to=1695131483277&var-interval=$__auto_interval_interval&var-node_name=fleet-d1&var-crop_host=fleet-d1&var-service_name=fleet-d1-mysql&var-version=5.7.28-31&var-crop_service=fleet-d1-mysq&var-environment=All&var-cluster=All&var-replication_set=All&var-database=All&var-node_type=All&var-service_type=All&var-username=All&var-schema=All] , there were two main spikes in a number of connections and a number of active threads.

!image-20230920-092655.png|width=91.66666666666667%!

16:47:38 ~ 16:47:39 A number of concurrent connections and a number of active threads went up from 1.114K to 2.81K within 1 second.

16:50:03 ~ 16:50:04 A number of concurrent connections and a number of active threads went up from 3.42K to 4.93K within 1 second.

If MySQL instance receives such a rapid number of connection requests in a short period of time, MySQL will stale and running 5K of active threads will definitely make MySQL instance a lot slower.

I will rule out the possibility of a disk performance issue because the disk was performing well at the given [timeframe|http://pmm2.sqldb/graph/d/node-disk/disk-details?orgId=1&var-interval=$__auto_interval_interval&var-node_name=fleet-d1&var-device=All&var-username=All&var-mountpoint=All&from=1695130624000&to=1695132436000].

EC2 instance has two 7,500G NVMe disks and is configured with RAID1 so in terms of read requests, it is as fast as RAID0.

As for [AHI|http://pmm2.sqldb/graph/d/mysql-innodb/mysql-innodb-details?orgId=1&from=1695130624000&to=1695132436000&var-interval=$__auto_interval_interval&var-node_name=fleet-d1&var-crop_host=fleet-d1&var-service_name=fleet-d1-mysql&var-version=5.7.28-31&var-crop_service=fleet-d1-mysq&var-environment=All&var-cluster=All&var-replication_set=All&var-database=All&var-node_type=All&var-service_type=All&var-username=All&var-schema=All], AHI add operation went up, but considering the ratio between AHI Total search and AHI Misses, it worked as expected.

* _We have provided our comments on the T&Cs based on the requirements under the ride-hailing regulation. We have tried to keep the original wording as much as possible and suggest edits/ amendments only to the clauses where strictly necessary. Please let us know if you require any assistance in this regard._
*  
*# _In relation to the_ *_Data Protection Policy_*_,_ _we understand that the document provided is for Bolt internal document (ie for Bolt’s personnel) as opposed to the policy using with Bolt’s customers._ +_May we reconfirm whether this [internal version] is the version which requires our review_+_? Upon receiving your reconfirmation, we will review the documents provided on an urgent basis (and kindly note that we have separately sent the email to Markul Hinterseer for the updated version)._
*  
_However, if it is not a correct version, please provide us with the updated version of Data Protection Policy (using with Bolt’s customers) for our review accordingly._
 
_In the meantime, we would like to provide our responses to your preliminary questions as follows:_
 
** _The ride hailing service provided by Bolt will be subject to the PDPA as this will be provided by the local entity. If Bolt Thailand will share the customer data with Bolt Estonia, Bolt Estonia may also be subject to the PDPA via Art 5(2)._
*  
** _We understand that Bolt Thailand (as the service provider) will also be the data controller. In such case, it will not be required to appoint any representative. The representative requirement may apply to Bolt Estonia if it will also be a data controller._
*  
** _Bolt can also use the global DPO based in Europe. The DPO should have the general knowledge of privacy laws and should be able to act promptly to contact with the regulator should there be any breach incident or complaint from customers. It is expected that the sub-regulation on the qualifications of the DPO will be announced after 1 June._
*  
** _In relation to your question on Article 29, we understand that you meant to ask about the requirements for the binding corporate rule (BCR)? In this case, the regulator has yet published any sub-regulation on this yet and it is expected to be published after 1 June. During the interim, the GDPR based data controller either (i) applies their existing GDPR standards or (ii) obtain consent for any data offshoring._
*  
*# _We would also like to bring your attention to the most recent change in the legal interpretation by the Office of Consumer Protection Bureau (OCPB) of the Direct Sales and Direct Marketing Act of Thailand (“_*_DSDM Act_*_”)._
*  
_Under the DSDM Act, any person operating a direct marketing business must obtain a license from the OCPB. ‘direct marketing’ means marketing of goods or services in the manner of communication of information in order to directly offer goods or services to consumers who are at a distance, with the aim of receiving a response by each customer to purchase the goods or services from such direct market operator._
 
_In the past, although the definition of “direct marketing” is broad enough to capture the offering of services, the DSDM Act has never been interpreted to apply to a “online sale of services” due to the issue over the interpretation that a ‘service’ cannot be returned as required under the DSDM Act. The regulator also interpreted that the DSDM Act did_ +_not_+ _apply to a platform service provider (such as Bolt app). Past attempt to apply for a direct marketing license by a platform service provider was unsuccessful._
 
_Nonetheless, there has been a change in the interpretation of the regulator within the past 4-6 months which was_ +_not_+ _published to the public. In the course of our assistance of another client, an online service provider that distributed its services through an app and website, it was determined by the regulator that a direct marketing license was also required for a online service. This is a significant change in the interpretation and how the OCPB enforces the DSDM Act that may also mandate another license for Bolt._
 
_We have not reached out to the regulator yet whether they have changed their interpretation for a platform provider (such as Bolt) as well. However, we have checked against the online system and found that Grab Taxi has just recently obtained this license in March. From the data base, we cannot ascertain whether this license was obtained by Grab Taxi_ +_for their ride hailing service_+ _or for any type of services (such as Grab Food, Mart or Express) which fits the traditional “sale of goods” that mandate the direct marketing license. We have not sighted a license obtained by LINE company but we cannot verify whether they are in the process of applying for this license._
 
_Please let us know if you would like us to proceed further and verify this point with the regulator on a no name basis. We note that a failure to obtain the direct marketing license may result in criminal liabilities under the DSDM Act.”_

Heyy, no worries, it took me some time to understand as well 😅 

So there are two types of Inactive Market tickets:

# The first type is when *we are not active either in the given country or in the city (for example, the US)* - these tickets stay in the specific Inactive Market queue in Beehive. At the moment those are handled by the UK Black Cabs team, but this can be changed in the future.
# The second type is when *we are active in the country but not in the city (the Dresden example)* - by default those tickets go to the local team’s (in this case Germany CS) backlog (as we have playmode on Beehive + it was requested from all teams to add Inactive Market filter on Beehive). Both Tier 1 and Tier 2 agents can handle those tickets. 
# As I understood from Jose’s message *not all Franchise markets have playmode enabled*, so some of their tickets can show up in the Inactive Market queue. 
In any case, *those tickets should still be handled by the local CS* and not the Inactive Market team (the UK Black Cabs team at the moment). Beehive does not have a way to exclude any certain markets when working on Inactive tier. Agents just need to be aware of what is active and franchise, and skip the tickets from these markets.

Let me know if you have more questions 🙌

{quote}PGP is not something we use.

Forced TLS is protocol-level encryption.

See the picture I sent earlier.

It is end-to-end encryption server-to-server not user-to-user

This means that for all users who send to and from between our domains, all e-mail is encrypted in transit after the servers have done the "handshake".

PGP uses private keys, and is not the same.

Forced TLS ensures that e-mail is encrypted until it reaches the recipient's inbox from the sender's inbox.

If additional encryption is desired, you can add things that are sent in a 7ZIP file with a password and AES encryption as an attachment, and then this will also be encrypted in the recipient's e-mail, where you can e.g. send password by SMS to recipient, for extra security.

Forced TLS is very secure, and has much less administration than PGP.

Forced TLS is always on, and only requires that all parties have valid SSL certificates on their mail servers.

For more info, see here: [https://www.egress.com/blog/email-encryption/opportunistic-tls-vs-forced-tls|https://www.egress.com/blog/email-encryption/opportunistic-tls-vs-forced-tls|smart-link]

Forced TLS must be set up with 1 of the parties in order for it to force encryption.

In general, mobile applications are designed to prevent one application from accessing or extracting data from other applications or the user's entire device without explicit user consent. Access to data, such as photos, contacts, or other apps, is controlled through a permission system. Here's how it works:

# Permission System: Mobile operating systems like Android (by Google) and iOS (by Apple) use a permission-based model. Each app must request specific permissions to access certain device features or data. Bolt doesn't request this access and doesn't collect this data.
# User Consent: When an app requests permission to access data or features, the user is typically presented with a permission request dialog. The user can choose to grant or deny the requested permission. Bolt doesn't request this access and doesn't collect this data.

*Why it's not possible without the user permission?*

# App Sandboxing: Mobile operating systems employ a technique called app sandboxing, which isolates each app in its own secure environment. This isolation prevents direct access to another app's data or processes.
# Data Encryption: Many mobile devices use encryption to protect data at rest (when stored on the device). This encryption ensures that even if an app were to gain access to data, it would be difficult to decrypt the data without the appropriate encryption keys.

*Step 1: Check for Fraudulent Patterns*

* The estimated distance and actual driven distance don’t match (the difference is above 20 km).
* The destination entered and ride finish locations are different.
* Drastic overcharge on a short trip.
* In the "Route points" tab on the order in Admin, check for "isSpeedDeltaTooFast" and "isDistanceDeltaTooBig" flags, indicating illogical speed calculations.
* Pay attention to multiple log-ins on the *Driver's Devices* during a single ride, as it may suggest possible fraudulent activities.

*Step 4 (Follow-up on the Report): GPS Spoofing*

* If automation was applied, inform the rider accordingly.
* If automation wasn't applied, compensate the overcharged amount with the Driver as a refund actor (deduct the refund amount from the driver’s earnings) and inform the rider accordingly.
* For cash trips, compensate the rider following your market rules.

*Step 5: Log the Report*

* If not already added, select the correct order from the Bolt Admin Panel. The report about the driver's behavior is now collected automatically.

*Step 6: Action the Report*

* If it's an isolated case, leave a comment on the order and close the ticket.
* If the driver has a history of multiple GPS overcharges, collect the cases and escalate to the Local OPS via Slack
* *Note*: Do not apply any manual blockings to the driver account. This is being handled only by the Local OPS.

h3. Example 1: correct 🆗 

* Rider has positive balance of 10, estimated price is 5, we authorized 5 from Balance and 0 from MoMo but final order price is 30
* Unpaid amount should be 20 (if at the end of ride we can adjust how much we get from BB)
* {{order_price - authorisation.BB - authorisation.PM - positive_balance_after_auth + ABS(negative_balance_pre_auth)}} will return 30 - 5 - 0 - 5 + 0 = 20
* The whole thing will be {{ABS(Math.Max(0, 20) = 20}}

h3. Example 2: correct 🆗 

* Rider has positive balance of 10, estimated price is 15, we authorized 10 from Balance and 5 from MoMo but final order price is 8
* Unpaid amount should be 0 (if at the end of ride we can adjust how much we get from BB)
* {{order_price - authorisation.BB - authorisation.PM - positive_balance_after_auth + ABS(negative_balance_pre_auth)}} will return 8 - 10 - 5 - 0 + 0 = -7
* The whole thing will be {{ABS(Math.Max(0, -7) = 0}}

h3. Example 3: correct 🆗

* Unpaid amount should be 0 
* {{order_price - authorisation.BB - authorisation.PM - positive_balance_after_auth + ABS(negative_balance_pre_auth)}} will return 7 - 0 - 25 - 0 + 10 = -8
* But the whole thing will be {{ABS(Math.Max(0, -8) = 0}}

* Unpaid amount should be 10
* {{order_price - authorisation.BB - authorisation.PM - positive_balance_after_auth + ABS(negative_balance_pre_auth)}} will return 25 - 0 - 25 - 0 + 10 = 10

{noformat}select 
etl.from_agent_vat_code as from_vat_code,
date_trunc('month', etl.created) as month,
count(distinct case when dm.is_bolt_market = true then etl.order_id end) as total_business_bolt_market_orders,
count(distinct etl.id) as total_invoices_issued,
sum(total_sum) as total_sum_loc,
sum(total_vat_sum) as total_vat_sum_loc,
sum(total_sum_with_vat) as total_sum_with_vat_loc,
sum(total_sum/cer.rate) as total_sum_eur,
sum(total_vat_sum/cer.rate) as total_vat_sum_eur,
sum(total_sum_with_vat/cer.rate) as total_sum_with_vat_eur
from ng_public.etl_billing_invoicing_delivery etl
left join ng_public.etl_delivery_order_monetary_metrics dm on dm.order_id = etl.order_id and dm.city_id = etl.city_id 
left join ng_public.business_invoicing_claim_data cd on cd.order_system_order_id = etl.order_id
left join ng_public.business_invoicing_claim c on c.id = cd.claim_id and c.type in ('delivery', 'delivery_courier_fee', 'delivery_food')
left join ng_public.currency_exchange_rates cer on cer.currency = etl.currency and cer.valid_on = DATE(etl.created)
where etl.from_agent_vat_code = 'RO37246510'
and etl.created >= DATE('2023-01-01')
and dm.is_bolt_market = true
and c.type in ('delivery_food')
group by 1,2,3{noformat}

Hey [~accountid:6052891960d39e006f72f0f0] and [~accountid:712020:f63df97f-cad1-4718-9bb1-80038488d7e2],

We had a call with Deniss today regarding this project.

*Timeframe for this project:* this is only the investigation stage on what the team can and cannot do from the privacy and legal perspective in case they decide to share some data with the suppliers. Once they understand our requirements, they will create an MVP and share it with us for the final review. 
*Privacy implications:* 

* The data will be shared in aggregated and anonymous for the supplier form. Most of the data are not of a personal data nature - such as city, products, etc. So the privacy legal team does not have concerns here. 
* Some data points have minor concerns (risk is low) for the users. These data include delivery location, age, and gender. We have agreed that for this data remains anonymous, there should not be any way for the suppliers to potentially identify the user from this data. It means that if we share these points, aggregated data should be rounded to a bigger location/metric so that it’s not possible to identify the users based on this info (not share exact addresses and share only region (East, West, etc.) or a bigger polygon of addresses, for age - bigger generalisation (users from 20-25, not users of 21 Y.O, etc)

Once the MVP is created and data points are defined, the team will share it with the privacy team to get final approval. In case of any doubts re data aggregation, the team will reach out to the privacy legal team.

[~accountid:6052891960d39e006f72f0f0] [~accountid:712020:f63df97f-cad1-4718-9bb1-80038488d7e2] , I propose that we create a privacy-legal document for such a project describing our high-level requirements and instructions in case of any issues. 
Moreover, for drafting the agreement with suppliers for selling this data (that are not of a personal nature since they are anonymised), our team would like to raise some issues:

* there should be a ban for the suppliers regarding the comms they made publicly. They should not state that Bolt sells any aggregated insight data since it can raise users' concerns regarding their privacy. 
* If there is a case when the suppliers want to make this communication, we need to assess it on a case-by-case basis and prepare our PR team and comms to be shared publicly.
* this data should not be re-sold or shared with other 3rd parties. Even if they are anonymous for a specific supplier (and we know the purposes and categories for this), we cannot be sure that the same set of data will be anonymous for other 3rd parties. It can create risks for user’s potential re-identification.

We also have TLS encryption to all @[gmail.com|http://gmail.com/] addresses, but we do not use cloud e-mail services.

 

It is physically impossible to do a Man-in-the-middle attack on a Force TLS encryption, since an ENCRYPTED VPN TUNNEL is created between SOURCE server and TARGET server HOSTS with Forced TLS encryption.

 

This means that the mail is sent through an encrypted tunnel from the source mail-server, to the destination mail server, even through any HOPS on the way, since all the connectivity's through the HOPS are done with an Encrypted VPN Tunnel. Hence you cannot tap into the connection in transit, since the tunnel is encrypted.

 

Your servers are using *Opportunistic* TLS configuration, which means both encrypted and non-encrypted e-mails on TLS levels are let through. E-mails only get encrypted if the other end has compatible encryption. *We have configured FORCED TLS*, meaning if an encrypted connection cannot be established prior to transferring the data, a connection is refused as an encrypted tunnel for transferring the data can not be created.

 

*Gmail* by default, _does not use Forced TLS encryption but Opportunistic TLS encryption_.

This means, if you have not specifically configured your Gmail connectors to force-encrypt e-mail, the e-mail is not being encrypted if the recipient has a non-encrypted security.

 

Best regards

and this does not work:

orders created comes from order table and requires 1 hop while orders_finished comes from order try table and requires 2 hops

Answer:

*Tom Lento (dbt labs)*  [8 minutes ago|https://getdbt.slack.com/archives/C02CCBBBR1D/p1695319955424559?thread_ts=1695289818.540139&cid=C02CCBBBR1D]


MetricFlow internally supports resolution and rendering of 2-hop joins with some substantive limitations (we do not allow fan-out steps and have no way to resolve ambiguous join paths at the moment). The interfaces for indicating that you want a multi-hop join are currently up in the air a bit because the original interfaces made it very difficult to add support for fanout joins and user-provided resolution of ambiguous join paths.We're working on resolving those interface issues and once we've got the base of a more extensible format it'll be documented and the feature will be useable from that point forward.If you run a query with something like {{order_id__customer__name}} in a group by, or {{{{ Dimension('customer__name', ['order_id']) }}}} in a filter expression we'll render a multi-hop join for you. But those query interfaces are under active development, so we haven't added them to the docs yet.

Emilie and I analyzed the letter received from the driver's lawyer.
The driver signed up on the app in 2019 and was working under fleet  In July 2023 he did not pass the selfie check verification due to the multiple device locations feature, launched without the necessary  legal reviews and safeguards. 
Even though the driver - wrongly - claims that he has never attempted to circumvent the app technology and rules, *he argues that we have brutally terminated an established commercial relationship and he is asking us to reactivate his account. For the time being, he’s not claiming damages.* 

+*A) Arguments in favour of the reactivation of driver’s account*+

# the driver *never received precise information on the verification mechanism.* The app currently requires you to take selfies. Nothing is specified about the location of the selfie and the capacity of the technology to detect geolocation.
# we are processing personal *geolocation data* without providing transparent information to drivers
# the driver has *never received an email* at the time of termination of his account illustrating the *reasons for immediate termination as per our T&Cs art 13.5 and FR commercial law requirement.* 
# Given the established nature of commercial relations (driver on the app since 2019) in case of +termination for convenience,+ the terminating party should provide prior written notice ( notice period depends on the duration of the commercial relationship, but according to FR Case law should not be less than 30 days - as reflected by the way in our T&Cs art. 13.4) . Failure of providing prior notice, the other party can claim damages in court. Although in this case we had +terminated the contract for breach+ ( not for convenience) of driver’s obligations according to our T&Cs ( impersonisation/ prêt de compte), +while terminating we infringed our T&Cs too since we didn’t notify the driver.+ *Therefore, there’s still a risk that the driver could lawfully claim damages (loss of profit and fees incurred) in court for brutal termination of established commercial relationship.* 
# When it comes to fleets, our current T&Cs are unclear and driver might claim that T*&Cs are not directly enforceable to him* but they are binding only upon the fleet owner. 
# On one side, the lawyer invoke commercial code provisions applying to a commercial relationship but on the other side, at the beginning of the letter, the language suggest some r*eclassification concerns raised by the lawyer and allegedly an established subordination link* . Hence, we cannot exclude that the lawyer will file a claim with the labour court. 

*B)*+*Arguments against the reactivation of driver’s account*+

* Our *credibility* and the consistency of our processes might be affected.
* *Risk of cascade effect* : all other 800-1000 drivers blocked for the same reason (ie selfie check verification/ multiple devices location could reach out to be reactivated) could reach out to reinstate their account. 

+*Conclusions*+

As just discussed and based on the above, +*I would suggest to reactivate the driver’s account*+ *and without waiting for the driver to bring the case to court whether commercial ( to claim damages) or labour court (to claim reclassification).* Of course, reactivation will be on the understanding that the driver should follow the rules and he might be blocked in the future if he tries to circumvent the platform. +We can give a second chance as we did not comply with our notification obligations, but we cannot disregard recidivism.+

Had a discussion about this task with Asia during our 1:1

* I explained that I did not detect any process logic issues, and all the steps are relevant / the order of them cannot be changed, etc. Due to this, I was also unable to find anything to work on
** I asked for feedback from Team Leads (and they asked their agents, both OS and IH), and only got the feedback mentioned in my previous comment. However, no examples were provided (they said they did not have examples), so we decided not to cover this scenario as it’s most likely an edge case. It was only mentioned by 2 markets with no examples.
* I did discover some things that could be improved when looking into the tickets with Jelena. For example:
** *When we refund a correctly charged fine for the 1st time, we should notify the user that we’re doing it as a 1st time exception to set clear expectations.* In some tickets, I noticed back-and-forth with riders who were charged the fine correctly, and were insisting on getting it refunded (while they had already been refunded previously). 
** *We should overall avoid going back-and-forth with riders, as in some tickets the rider kept coming back to us.* If we’ve concluded the investigation and see that compensation/refund is not necessary, agents should be able to use their soft skills to end the conversation.
** Some agents tried to end the conversation with smth like “unfortunately due to our compensation policy, we cannot refund the fine”. We should avoid saying that bc “compensation policy” is quite an abstract expression (e.g. the rider might ask where can they see the policy then). Instead, we can end the conversation with something like “we’ve looked into this and this is the solution we can offer you”. 
** Some agents were not following the process (they didn’t refund the fine if it was the 1st time charged). 

Next steps:

* Highlight the bullet points above to the QA and Training team
* Mention to SC the fact that we should inform riders when refunding the 1st correctly charged fine that it won’t be done in the future (to add a note to the [process|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360008729834#h_01GJ08DJZQQKMC84TY6NV8YXQB], step 1 under “fine charged correctly”)

When it comes to the relationship between fleets and couriers, there are several types of employment contracts that fleets can conclude with their couriers:

* Individual employment contract for an indefinite period;
* Individual fixed-term employment contract;

—--

* Full time contract
* Part-time contract

Also, the _Civil Code_ allows collaboration contracts, as follows:

* collaboration contract with withholding tax
* copyright agreement
* service contract

Collaboration contracts can be concluded with:

* individuals who earn income from independent activities: income from copyrights, liberal professions (lawyer, doctor, nurse, financial consultant, etc.)
* PFA (natural authorised person), PFI, II, IF, SRL (limited liability company)
