*When will we know more?*

* The proposition was submitted by the Government to the Riksdag (supreme decision-making authority in Sweden) on 5 September 2023. Deadline for submitting motions is 27 September (opinions from individuals, NGOs, other authorities, and other stakeholders).
* There is a plan set up for preparation with respect to this proposition in the committee, on 10 October. The committee is an expert group that proposes to the Riksdag how the Riksdag should decide on specific issues.
* After the committee has submitted their proposal to the Riksdag, there is a debate in the Riksdag, then the final decision is made. Therefore, we can probably expect to see the final decision sometime in November, i.e., about a month after the committee has submitted their proposal to the Riksdag.

*What are the chances of the proposition not being enacted?*
It should be noted that the proposition is based on a new EU Directive which requires certain minimum levels of expansion of the scope of the member states' local law MTPL insurance requirements by 23 December at the lates. However, the proposed amendments to Swedish law as set forth in the proposition are far more extensive than the minimum level required under the Directive. It is even stated in the introduction of the Directive that the new rules are not meant to cover lighter or smaller vehicles as including them "_would also undermine the uptake of newer vehicles, such as electric bicycles that are not exclusively propelled by mechanical power, and discourage innovation_".It is uncommon for propositions to become subject to any material changes once submitted to the Riksdag, although, the fact that the amendments to Swedish law suggested in the proposition are so far reaching compared to what is required in the Directive may increase our chances a little bit. It is very difficult to say, but all in all I would not get my hopes up too much.

Dear [~accountid:5d5ff2f8c6318a0d6cd6ca21] 

Thank you for providing the additional information. It seems to me like the user is indeed guilty of illegal parking of the scooter, and thus, has committed a breach of our T&Cs, which would entitle us to claim payment for the parking fine from the user. 

However, our legal ability to pass through fines to users provides that we have the technical capabilities to ensure that the user receiving the penalty fee is the one responsible for the illegal parking. In other words, we still need to be able to prove that the user is guilty of the illegal parking, as this constitutes the breach of our T&Cs, which is the basis for our right to claim payment from the user. 

In light of this, please see a summary of my assessment of the circumstances in this case below.

*1. The legal basis for our claim is the breach of our T&Cs - not the fine issued by Stockholm stad*

First, it should be noted that it is not Stockholm stad that issues the fine to the user directly. It is Stockholm stad that issues the fine to us, and we then forward the fine onto the user. It should also be noted that the attached document is not, legally speaking, a parking "fine" but simply a protocol of the procedure of collecting vehicles which have been illegally parked. To retrieve the vehicles from the depot Bolt has to pay the impounding charges for the relocation of the vehicles. 

Given that fines are not issued by Stockholm stad directly to users (see above), I recommend arguing from the point of view that our claim is based on that the illegal parking is a breach of our T&Cs (which the user has agreed to comply with) - rather than arguing that the user has no choice but to pay the fine since Stockholm stad issued the fine to the user (which, again, is not true). Illegal parking is a breach of our T&Cs, and this is the basis for any right we may have to pass any claim relating to the illegal parking onto the user.

*2. Using the document from Stockholm stad as evidence*

The documents that we receive from Stockholm stad can often be used as evidence, e.g., if the pictures therein match the end of ride-picture taken by the user. However, if the evidence provided in the document from Stockholm stad is not sufficient to prove that the user has committed a breach of our T&Cs, e.g., because the user did not take any end of ride-picture to match with, it is _our_ responsibility to present better evidence to substantiate our claim. One way of doing this is connecting the pictures received from Stockholm stad with our GPS data, just like you just did in your last comment in this ticket.

*3. Using the document from Stockholm stad together with our GPS data as evidence*

I don’t know whether we typically disclose to users that we have GPS data showing where they parked the vehicle, but unless this is prohibited for some reason (please check standard procedure with your team if you are unsure), I recommend explaining to the user that we have evidence in the form of GPS data showing that the vehicle was parked in the same spot as shown in the pictures from Stockholm stad, just like you explained to me in your last comment in this ticket.

*4. Assessment of our collective evidence in this case*

The “strength” of our evidence is difficult for me to assess, since it depends on how reliable the GPS data is, which I do not know. Unless the GPS data is generally very unreliable, my assessment is that what we have enough evidence to show that the user parked the vehicle in a manner contrary to our T&Cs, which entitles us to claim payment of the parking fine from the user.

Please let me know if you have any further questions, or if there is anything else I can help sorting out from a legal perspective. Otherwise, please let me know if I can close the ticket.

Best regards,

Ida

Non-competition clause is the element of employment relationship and is also regulated by Employment Contract act in Estonia. EE Service contract template with natural person available here: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/3959718377/Employment+Contract+or+Contract+of+Services+with+a+natural+person#7.-Templates-%F0%9F%93%84-%E2%9D%97|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/3959718377/Employment+Contract+or+Contract+of+Services+with+a+natural+person#7.-Templates-%F0%9F%93%84-%E2%9D%97|smart-link] don’t have such clause and it is stated that in general such clause cannot be agreed, because it is considered as restricting free market trade that may lead to violation of competition laws. Contractor has the freedom to work for several clients of their own choice. 

On the other hand service contract is based on a free will and parties are relatively free to agree on any clauses they want as long as it is in compliance with the legal requirements. I am currently discussing this with EE lawyer and will post an update here afterwards.

Hi [~accountid:6012ab10dc29b4006a594649] 

I have reviewed the agreement and made a , please see below an executive summary of my assessment, as well as a list providing more details on some key findings in the agreement.

*Executive summary*

In summary, the agreement presents several red flags and is overall unacceptable in its current form. It lacks key clauses that must be included in any agreement, maybe even more important in a consultancy agreement, such as providing a clear scope, non-compete, liability, and protection of Bolt’s proprietary information and intellectual property, are missing. Also, the clauses that are actually in the agreement, e.g, the contract term, termination, fee, and scope, are either contradictory to one another, or severely unclear, to the extent that not having any written agreement _at all_ would provide better protection of Bolt’s interests than this agreement (although neither provides the protection we require). I do *not* recommend signing this agreement unless the consultant agrees to substantial amendments to protect Bolt’s interests.

Please see further details of key issues identified below. 

The following points may warrant further negotiation:

# *Unclear term:* There are two different effective dates stated in the agreement: section 1.2 “Time and availability” states that the agreement is valid from the day it is signed for both parties - while section 3.1 “Terms” states that the agreement comes into effect August 2023. In addition, regarding the end date, the two different clauses state (in chronological order) that the agreement is “planned” to continue until the application to the City of Oslo is submitted, while the latter states that the agreement “shall continue in full force and effect until the application to the City of Oslo is submitted”. 
# *Unclear scope of assignment:* Section 1.2 states that Bolt has the right to decide the scope of the assignment, while section 3.1 states that “The Client and the Supplier may negotiate the extension of the duration of this agreement and the terms under which the relationship will continue”. Although the latter does not explicitly entail that the agreement scope may be wider than as stated in the agreement, subject to other oral agreements entered during negotiations outside of the four walls of the written agreement - it may be interpreted as just that. 
# *Generous reimbursements of travel expenses etc.*: Reimbursement of travel costs etc. is regulated in clause 2.2. The language is so broad that the clause would basically cover any expense that the Supplier may have in connection with the agreement, including expenses related to just commuting to work. It should in any event be clear in the agreement that any such expenses must be documented, reasonable and motivated solely for the purpose of completing the assignment. 
# *The fee*: The fee of NOK 1,750 per month needs to be clarified. There is no mention of how many hours or what services exactly this covers, whether it is a flat fee or a per hour fee, or what is included. 
# *Short payment term:* Payment term is only 14 days from the date of invoicing by the Supplier. Should be 30 days.
# *Disadvantageous termination clause*: In section 3.2, as it currently stands, termination due to deficiencies requires written warning and a chance for the Supplier to rectify them. The process for identifying and rectifying deficiencies in the Supplier's delivery is unclear, which means that we may end up in a dispute of whether or not we have the right to terminate the agreement even if the Supplier does not live up to minimum expectations. Also, we need to have the opportunity of terminating the agreement with immediate effect in the event of consistent or serious deficiencies, especially for material breaches of the Supplier’s obligations, confidentiality breaches, etc.
# *Agreement generally favorable for the Supplier, e.g. no penalties*: It’s common for the Supplier to have all sorts of liabilities in these types of Supplier agreements (time-sensitive, clear goal), especially in such an information-sensitive and hot business as Bolt (lots of competition, benchmarking etc). There should be liquidated damages, indemnities and a right for Bolt to terminate for convenience. We need the best of the best on this.
# *Confidentiality concerns*: The agreement refers to a separate confidentiality agreement. We should ensure that the terms of this agreement are satisfactory and provide sufficient protections for Bolt's proprietary information. Also, the “ownership of products” clause in section 1.4 is _extremely broad_. We can *not* accept that the Supplier owns _everything_ they produce for us, and is thus free to bring anything they like to the next client - both from a business- and confidentiality perspective.

In light of the above, using the Supplier’s template would require substantial amendments to be made for Bolt’s interests to be considered sufficiently protected and for us to be able to approve any signing of the agreement from a legal perspective. 

An alternative (and more effective way of going about this) would be agreeing to use Bolt’s template instead, which already includes the necessary language and protection of our interests that we need. Therefore, I recommend sending our template over to It’s Tomorrow and suggest that we use that as our basis for negotiation instead.

Please let me know your thoughts on this and if you have any questions.

Best regards,

Ida

Exmo Senhores

Venho por este meio comunicar a minha situação, na qual estou a sofrer uma pequena Extorsão por parte da Bolt. Sou utilizador de trotinetes desta referida empresa. Como tal, sempre cumpri as regras de utilização, pagamento e manutenção da mesma.

Entretanto no dia 31 de julho de 2023, aluguei uma trotinete na Estação de Entrecampos, como sempre fiz. E desloquei-me para o meu trabalho, na Av. 5 de Outubro, aonde em frente, sempre estacionei a trotinete por mim usada, pois é um parque devidamente assinalado para o mesmo

. A aplicação da Bolt neste dia não quis efetuar o término da minha viagem, alegando que o parque não estava correto, o que é falso, sendo que como referi, sempre estacionei no mesmo lugar. Tentei ir a outro parque na Av. Duque D'Avila, e sucedeu-se o mesmo. Ou seja, a recusa da Aplicação da referida empresa, em terminar a minha viagem.

Tentei comunicar com a Bolt, que aliás é extremamente difícil de realizar, e não obtive nenhuma resposta imediata .Fiz uma reclamação a posteriori, enviei fotos, vídeos de como estava a minha situação, e a reposta é sempre a mesma, de que eu como utilizador estou incorreto.

Conclusão, está a ser-me cobrado 15,00€ por uma viagem de 1 hora, sendo que, só realizei uma viagem de 9 a 10 minutos que custaria 1,90€, como o meu próprio relatório de viagens pode confirmar. É lamentável esta situação que causou-me problemas com a cliente que iria atender neste dia, e também com deslocações ao meu Banco , para tentar evitar esta cobrança Abusiva.

Espero ter esta situação resolvida o mais breve possível. Desde já os meus mais sinceros agradecimentos.

Com os melhores cumprimentos

Wagner dos Santos Conceção

{{Case 2}}: Scheduled orders are trying to consume the campaign quite a while after locking the campaign. It could be up to 60 hours, IIRC. Looking at the logs I’ve noticed we’re getting a {{NO_DISCOUNT_CALCULATION (4523400)}} error from the Campaign system when trying to lock such campaign.

{{Case 3}}: Those baskets seem to be stuck in authorisation phase where we’re waiting for a token from the user. We have a cron that would cancel such processes after a given time, but something seems to not be working. I’ll investigate.

Hi Naomi,

The issue you're facing might be related to the format of the document, compatibility issues, or possibly an issue with your internet connection. 

Here's a step-by-step guide to help you troubleshoot and resolve the problem:

# *Check File Format*:
#* Make sure the IRP5 document you downloaded is in a compatible format. The most common formats for tax documents are PDF and sometimes CSV. If it's not in the correct format, consider converting it to PDF.
# *Document Opening Test*:
#* Open the IRP5 document on your Mac and verify that it displays correctly. Ensure that the content is visible and legible. This will help confirm if the issue is with the document itself or the process of sending/uploading.
# *Document Size*:
#* Check the file size of the IRP5 document. Extremely large files may have trouble uploading. If it's too large, consider compressing it into a ZIP file or splitting it into smaller parts if that's allowed.
# *Use a Different Browser*:
#* If you're trying to upload the document to eFiling using a web browser, try using a different one. Sometimes, browser-specific issues can cause problems. For example, if you were using Safari, try using Google Chrome or Mozilla Firefox.
# *Check Internet Connection*:
#* Ensure that your internet connection is stable and has sufficient bandwidth to upload/download files. A slow or unstable connection can cause files to fail to upload or download.
# *Update Software*:
#* Ensure that your operating system and web browsers are up to date. Sometimes, outdated software can lead to compatibility issues.
# *Clear Cache and Cookies*:
#* Clear your browser's cache and cookies. Accumulated data can sometimes interfere with the proper functioning of web applications.
# *Try a Different Device*:
#* If possible, try accessing eFiling and uploading the IRP5 document from a different device (e.g., a Windows PC or a different Mac). This can help determine if the issue is specific to your Mac or more widespread.
# *eFiling Compatibility*:
#* Ensure that the eFiling platform you're using is compatible with Mac. Some platforms have specific requirements or limitations when used on Mac computers.
# *Contact Support*:
#* If you've tried all the steps above and the issue persists, reach out to the eFiling support team for assistance. They may have specific insights or solutions for your situation.

By following these steps, you should be able to diagnose and resolve the issue you're experiencing when sending or uploading your IRP5 document. Remember to keep backup copies of your documents before attempting any troubleshooting steps to avoid accidental data loss.


Kind regards,
Liezl Schreuder

Hey, [~accountid:712020:0641ea87-e832-482b-8673-ab85e9ad6441]! I have reviewed this ticket and I would like your opinion of whether my intended approach is correct before I reply to CS.

I believe that there is no reason to report the rider’s behaviour to the police because Bolt acts as an intermediary and any police reports shall be made by drivers if they feel doing so. Bolt has no ground to make a report. I would suggest doing the following:

# Gather information on whether there is a proven record of drivers refusing service to riders with special assistance dogs. If there is a record of such refusals we may need to send a reminder to the drivers that they should accept riders with special assistance dogs.
# Assess whether there are any grounds for blocking the rider according to our T&Cs. Bolt has right to block the rider if rider breaches the Acceptable Use Rules, T&Cs or if it is necessary to protect the integrity of Bolt or Drivers, in particular in the event of crime. Initially, it is important to assess Acceptable Use Rules that are in the section 12 of the [T&Cs|https://assets.ctfassets.net/tk7rwcciwvbq/2z1LDv5HQEtZ4kjquemxjD/82313332068d99f196212e9245b7c650/Terms_and_Conditions_for_Passengers__valid_as_of_01.05.2023_.docx.pdf] and identify any grounds for blocking (probably 12.2 (d) and (l)). Unless drivers (or other third parties) will successfully report the rider to the police and the rider receives a criminal charge for an offence - Bolt cannot really assume that a crime was committed by the rider. Also, there is the [Bad Rider Management feature|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PRODWIKI/pages/4507959691/Bad+Rider+Management] that allows to suspend rider based on violation of these [Marketplace Conduct Guidelines: Riders|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/marketplace-guidelines-terms/]. It could potentially help in this case, but it seems that it was not implemented in the Portuguese T&Cs and although the rider has accepted the terms of the guidelines when they signed up it is not guaranteed that courts will accept that rider has consented to these guidelines. Therefore it is risky to apply Bad Rider Management feature in this case as the case may end up in court.
# Since this is a sensitive case we need to be careful with our approach towards the rider. We may need to approach the rider and explain that special assistance dogs are permitted according to our policy, but drivers make their own decisions and therefore we cannot guarantee that special assistance dogs will be admitted, although we have taken steps to remind drivers that special assistance dogs should be admitted.

I can confirm that the technical changes have been executed, to add Mihkel as a *reviewer* on the Requisition Business Process. This means that whenever a requisition is raised by COPS team, Mihkel will be able to *review* this as a first point of call, then it will go for *approval.* 

The reason why I am differentiating between review and approval, is approval is an official business process step that should always match against a budget holder. Review is a set of eyes reviewing something, before it is approved. This is particuarly important in audit processes where we may get questioned by external auditors, and for IPO standard. 

I am also highlighting here that this is for requisitions only, because POs don’t need a second approval once a requisition has been approved, unless qty/unit price have changed therefore only budget owners should have that responsibility. You can always add Mihkel there on POs as approver via ad-hoc approve button if you felt the need too. 

Please note, that the system does not allow for back-dating of exisiting transactions, so it will only be relevant for new requisitions submitted from now on. Thanks!

Hello [~accountid:641d5e830e6828ab20269e6d] ,

Could you please check these comments and bring some answers to the questions presented? I would initially say that we don’t need a DPIA, but I’ll be sure only after these aspects are clarified – most importantly, the fact that the business intends to install an app from a third party to couriers’ phones.

# The privacy notice of the provider does not stand up to the minimum standards of a privacy notice: [https://www.truemetrics.io/imprint-disclaimer-privacy#privacy.|https://www.truemetrics.io/imprint-disclaimer-privacy#privacy.|smart-link]  This should be seen as a red flag when engaging with the provider.
# It’s stated in the document that the provider’s features include “advanced activity recognition, distinguishing between activities such as standing still, walking, cycling, vehicle use, climbing stairs, and using elevators.” Although it’s a business secret, it’s important to understand what kind of data they collect or process to come to such a fine-tuned classification, especially if this kind of information will be used by Bolt at any point in the project. What I mean is, if supposedly the project just collects GPS location, are we, as controllers, sure that they do not collect any other categories of data through their app?
# It’s stated in the document that only location data will be used. Are we sure no other category of personal data will be used, such as identity data or contact details data? If we’re selecting couriers “A”, “B”, and “C”, I would say that we would be using at least their names and contacts.
# The document mentions the following purposes: “Building entrance detection: if couriers enter a building, the sensors will be able to tell when the person switches from outdoor to indoor location”; “Detailed delivery time segments (Walking, Biking, Vehicle time segments)”; “Parking spot detection: the place where a courier state change occurs (Vehicle → Walking)”; and “Raw and processed GPS traces”. What categories of data will be used to achieve such purposes? Also, how will this data be linked to any courier - if it will? If such a connection between data and courier exists, we would be able to track every single step of the courier, which seems something we have to be worried about.
# If we’ll be asking our couriers to install the app on their phones, the only possible legal basis would be consent. I’m inferring that we’ll be doing this because this is the option highlighted in the document (“Demo application that can be temporarily installed on the Courier’s phone that they use for Bolt deliveries.”)
# What data exactly will be sent to the provider? For me, it seems it won’t be only GPS data.
# In relation to couriers’ rights, if the business decides to use consent, all rights must be guaranteed, except for the right to object.
# The installation of a third-party app on our couriers’ phones should be thoroughly evaluated. What data is collected through the app? What are the identifiers this app collects? It’s not clear what the third party will do with such data - and I’m not talking about deletion, since above it was stated that the data would be deleted, but I’m concerned with other uses the provider may have with the data collected from our couriers.
# About the retention period: if the collected data could be anonymized, then there would be no problem. However, if data can’t be anonymized (or if the business doesn’t want to anonymize), then an explicit period of time must be defined. Also, if this is just a project for us to compare with our own systems, there seems to be no reason to keep the data indefinitely.
# On security, as Bolt seems to opt to install an app from a third-party provider, for sure personal data will be involved. Also, there’s no mention of which security measures (technical and organizational) will be applied in the project, both those from Bolt and those from the provider. This needs to be clear before moving on with this project.

Thank you for clarifying.

Finished the review, but cannot post a note for the customer. Leaving the outcome of the review here for future reference:

It seems that this contract presumes that Bolt will be issuing vouchers and MyBenefit will act as an intermediary only providing its platform so as persons could get access to Bolt’s vouchers. MyBenefit makes it clear that Bolt will be the issuer and seller of the vouchers. They define vouchers as an instrument enabling users to make a pre-payment for a certain product or service offered by Bolt. The contract states that the voucher will be paid for first and then the user will be able to redeem it. Therefore, it is the same definition that Bolt uses for vouchers [+here+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/4543447872/Coupons+and+vouchers.+Bolt+Business+Legal]. Since the payment for the voucher will be done before it will be redeemed, i.e. before the service will be used, Bolt will be considered as an issuer of “electronic money” and this activity requires a licence that Bolt does not have. Therefore, we are unable to issue vouchers and enter into this contract.

Bolt is planning to introduce Bolt Food into the Bolt Business logic and also add a Company Dashboard that will enable business customers to issue coupons for their employees. Perhaps this particular use case will be a good fit for that upcoming solution?

*How to password-protect a file and folder on Windows*



You can create *a password-protected ZIP archive.* Here's a step-by-step guide:

*Step 1. Select the File*

Locate the file you want to protect.

*Step 2. Right-Click on the File*

Right-click on the file to bring up the context menu.

*Step 3. Select "Send to"*

From the context menu, select "Send to" and then choose "Compressed (zipped) folder”. 

*Step 4. Rename the ZIP Archive*

A ZIP archive with the same name as your file will be created in the same folder. You can rename this archive if you like.

*Step 5. Open the ZIP Archive*

Double-click on the newly created ZIP archive to open it.

*Step 6. Set a Password*

In the ZIP archive window, click the "File" menu, and select "Set Password."

*Step 7. Enter the Password*

Enter the password you want to use to protect the ZIP archive. Make sure it's a strong and secure password.

*Step 8. Confirm the Password*

Confirm the password by entering it again.

*Step 9. Apply Password*

Click the "OK" button to apply the password to the ZIP archive.

*Step 10. Add Files to the ZIP Archive*

Drag and drop the file you want to protect into the ZIP archive window.

*Step 11. Close the ZIP Archive*

Close the ZIP archive window.

Now, your file is securely protected within the password-protected ZIP archive. To access the file, you'll need to open the ZIP archive and enter the password when prompted. 

*Note:* Ensure that you remember the password you set, as there is no way to recover it if it is forgotten.

HI [~accountid:61124fbaec92ab0070270a0b] as a summary of our previous discussion please see below:

* +How do you see this initiative from a reclassification stand point?+

Courts seem to understand that providing training is one of the powers (in addition to orientation, supervision, discipline and monitoring) configuring a relation of subordination between an employee and employer. Hence, giving away free courses would appear to increase the reclassification risk. 

Particularly risky would be providing payment directly to drivers of these courses. In our recent experience with the Labour Inspector, one of the elements requested were invoices related with couriers. Hence, I would recommend avoiding financial transfer directly to drivers, such as by paying a language course.

However, collaborating with course providers in the context of Bolt Offers for discounts would appear less of a risk.

* +Can we phrase this as a marketing initiative?+

In labour law the analysis of courts are normally factual and therefore I would not see any impact in phrasing it as a marketing initiative.

* +Having absolutely no connection with performance, access to the platform, benefits, etc. what do you believe is the risk of this being used to prove the training criteria?+

On one side, courts in Portugal seem to understand that providing training is one of the powers (in addition to orientation, supervision, discipline and monitoring) configuring a relation of subordination between an employee and employer. 

On the other side, the Supreme Court understands that the fact that an individual “receives training and is subject to general guidelines and suggestions … does not in itself mean legal subordination, because in the provision of services, the person who hires can also organize, supervise and monitor their provision with a view to controlling the result.” 

Even though, training by itself may not trigger reclassification, the concern is that providing free language courses in addition to other factual  *s*ituations (real time monitoring of activity and blocking) may lead to the fulfilment of 2 or more reclassification criteria. 

Therefore I understand that providing language courses to drivers may increase the risk of reclassification for Bolt.

* +Also considering it is totally optional and it would be for driver who demonstrate interest?+

I believe this is a measure to mitigate risk, but there is a reclassification risk. Please see previous comment.

As a *conclusion*, I believe providing free courses to drivers would appear to increase the risk of reclassification and would not recommend it, except for the discount available in Bolt Club as other offers already available. Particularly risky would be paying the training directly to the drivers, since invoices is the type of documentation requested in labour inspections.

It seems that this contract presumes that Bolt will be issuing vouchers and MyBenefit will act as an intermediary only providing its platform so as persons could get access to Bolt’s vouchers. MyBenefit makes it clear that Bolt will be the issuer and seller of the vouchers. They define vouchers as an instrument enabling users to make a pre-payment for a certain product or service offered by Bolt. The contract states that the voucher will be paid for first and then the user will be able to redeem it. Therefore, it is the same definition that Bolt uses for vouchers [+here+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/4543447872/Coupons+and+vouchers.+Bolt+Business+Legal]. Since the payment for the voucher will be done before it will be redeemed, i.e. before the service will be used, Bolt will be considered as an issuer of “electronic money” and this activity requires a licence that Bolt does not have. Therefore, we are unable to issue vouchers and enter into this contract.

I understand that MyBenefit is popular in Poland and perhaps they are aware of how this electronic money licence issue is solved. Perhaps you can consult with them?

Also, Bolt is planning to introduce Bolt Food into the Bolt Business logic and also add a Company Dashboard that will enable business customers to issue coupons for their employees. Perhaps this particular use case will be a good fit for that upcoming solution?

* {{delete account}} and {{change email}} are not _that_ sensitive actions (e.g they could be at most be used for griefing and surveillance, since bills seem to be sent to address listed under email info)
* {{change phone}} seems to be actually privileged action, but due to long user sessions the number can be out of date so reauthentication might be impossible.

I agree with [@aleksei.valiakin|https://taxify.slack.com/team/UKLKEB7C4] that decision on the risk management should be made by the product team. It seems that the decision on further action depends heavily on topics discussed in [#feature-auth-loopholes|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C05P3NPE43Z]. Anyhow  as there is no quick fix for these issues, so my recommendation on behalf of infosec would be to focus on the long term fixes.

TL;DR Infosec has gained some insight into the issue and we do not see any point in rushing out partial solutions to these issues, let's focus on the long term mitigations instead. We can always apply band-aid if this becomes a problem.
